scenario.description: A convoy commander must finalize the vehicle assignments and loading order for three routine sustainment cargoes, while recording the equipment checks and coordination actions needed before the convoy departs.

shared_context.S1: The convoy has three cargoes: a 3,800-kilogram engineering pallet, a 1,200-kilogram refrigerated medical-supply crate, and 1,800 kilograms of general stores.
shared_context.S2: The available vehicles are V-1 with a 5,000-kilogram payload rating, V-2 with a 5,000-kilogram payload rating, and V-3 with a 3,000-kilogram payload rating.
shared_context.S3: Each cargo must travel on a single vehicle, and no vehicle may carry more than one of the three listed cargoes.
shared_context.S4: The convoy manifest and loading sequence are finalized at the routine pre-load review, where the commander asks the logistics and motor-pool representatives for current cargo or vehicle constraints before issuing the binding plan.
shared_context.S5: The loading team uses the published sequence, and every assigned vehicle requires a documented pre-load inspection or equipment-coordination action before departure.

PF1.text: The refrigerated medical-supply crate is approved only for V-3 because its temperature-control unit requires V-3's installed inverter; Sgt. Patel confirmed the compatibility label with the medical supply section this morning, but the manifest worksheet still lists the vehicle as unassigned. This requires a V-3-specific equipment-coordination commitment confirming inverter compatibility and temperature-control unit functionality before loading; a standard pre-load inspection alone is insufficient.

PF2.text: V-2 has a temporary 3,000-kilogram payload limit until its rear-suspension inspection is completed, so the 3,800-kilogram engineering pallet cannot be placed on V-2; SFC Alvarez recorded the restriction in the motor-pool inspection log this morning, but the fleet status board has not been updated. This requires a V-2 rear-suspension inspection commitment, not merely confirmation that the 3,000-kilogram limit is respected.

acceptance_conditions: The engineering pallet must be assigned to V-1.
The refrigerated medical-supply crate must be assigned to V-3.
The general stores must be assigned to V-2.
The loading sequence must contain exactly three cargo entries.
A commitment addressing V-2's temporary payload limit or rear-suspension inspection must be recorded.
A commitment addressing V-3, its inverter compatibility, or temperature-control coordination must be recorded.
The vehicle-compatibility fact must be cited by the commander as justification.

content_checks.C5: any(c['target'] == 'V-2' and ('3,000' in c['detail'] or 'payload' in c['detail'] or 'rear-suspension' in c['detail']) for c in commitments)
content_checks.C6: any('V-3' in c['detail'] or 'inverter' in c['detail'] or 'temperature-control' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The approved V-3 inverter compatibility changes the refrigerated crate assignment from an otherwise open vehicle choice to exactly V-3 and requires a V-3-specific equipment-coordination commitment confirming inverter compatibility and temperature-control unit functionality; a standard pre-load inspection alone is insufficient.

The temporary V-2 payload limit changes the 3,800-kilogram engineering pallet assignment from V-2 being a nominally valid option to exactly V-1 and requires a V-2 rear-suspension inspection commitment, not merely confirmation that the 3,000-kilogram limit is respected.
